short_term.title: Get AWS Cloud Practitioner Certification
short_term.description: AWS is the market leader (4 of 9 postings require it) and you currently have only Azure. The AWS Cloud Practitioner is the foundational cert; it costs $100 USD and typically requires 20–30 hours of study. Study materials are free via freeCodeCamp (YouTube) or Tutorialsdojo practice exams. Exam is 65 questions in 90 minutes. Schedule the exam within 4–5 weeks. This immediately closes a major gap and signals cloud versatility.

short_term.title: Complete TypeScript fundamentals tutorial
short_term.description: TypeScript is increasingly required alongside JavaScript (5 postings mention JS/TS). Complete the free 'Beginners TypeScript Tutorial' from Total TypeScript (https://www.totaltypescript.com/learn-typescript) or Scrimba's 'Learn TypeScript' free course (4.2 hours, certificate included). This gives you baseline TypeScript literacy to pair with your JavaScript foundation, making you more competitive for full-stack roles.

short_term.title: Build a small REST API project in TypeScript or Go
short_term.description: Create a simple portfolio project that demonstrates REST API design with proper HTTP verbs, resource naming, and endpoints. Use either: (a) TypeScript/Node.js with Express or Fastify (leverages your Python/FastAPI knowledge to a new stack), or (b) Go (hits both the Go gap and REST API gap simultaneously). ~2–3 weeks part-time effort. This becomes a portfolio piece you can show employers and simultaneously closes two gaps.

medium_term.title: Learn Go fundamentals and build a production-like project
medium_term.description: Go appears in 3 of 9 postings and is a gap. Use free resources: Codecademy's 'Learn Go' (free course, 2–4 hours intro), then build a microservice or CLI tool that demonstrates: structs, interfaces, concurrency basics, and proper error handling. Aim for a GitHub-hosted, well-documented project. ~4–6 weeks part-time. This directly addresses Go gap and positions you for backend/DevOps roles where Go is increasingly used (cloud tooling, microservices).

medium_term.title: Learn React fundamentals with a small portfolio project
medium_term.description: React appears in 3 postings as a frontend skill. You have JavaScript but no React. Start with Egghead.io's 'Beginners Guide to ReactJS' (free) or Scrimba's 'Learn React for free' (48 video tutorials, hands-on), then build a small project (e.g., a todo app, weather dashboard, or portfolio site) using React. ~3–4 weeks part-time (15–20 hours). Deploy it to Vercel or GitHub Pages. This makes you more competitive for full-stack roles and closes a visible gap.

medium_term.title: Complete Java fundamentals course and build a practice project
medium_term.description: Java appears in 3 postings. Using free resources (MyGreatLearning's 'Java Programming' free course or Bro Code's YouTube 'Java Full Course for Beginners'), learn Java fundamentals (15–20 hours), then build a small project (e.g., a command-line app, simple data structure implementation, or REST API in Spring Boot). ~4–5 weeks part-time. This signals backend versatility and closes the Java gap.

long_term.title: Pursue a Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or equivalent
long_term.description: 6 of 9 postings explicitly require or expect a Bachelor's degree in CS or related field. You have an Advanced Diploma in Computer Programming & Analysis, which demonstrates technical competency but may be flagged by some recruiters or ATS systems. Consider: (1) a part-time/online BS in CS (e.g., University of Waterloo's Online BASc, University of Toronto's iSchool, or Athabasca University), (2) a formal bootcamp with recognized credentials, or (3) building a strong portfolio of real-world projects and contributions (open source, published papers, deployed systems) that compensate for the credential gap. This is a long-term consideration; prioritize short/medium-term skill gaps first, then revisit this as your career progresses. Estimated duration: 2–4 years part-time for a degree, or 1–2 years via bootcamp + portfolio building.

summary: You're well-positioned as an early-career developer with standout AI/ML and DevOps experience. Your hands-on work with RAG pipelines, microservices modernization, and infrastructure automation directly align with current market demand, and your technical depth (GitOps, security-first CI/CD, vector databases) is rare for entry-level candidates. However, you face two strategic gaps: (1) breadth across the modern full-stack ecosystem — AWS is a major gap (you're Azure-focused), and Go, React, and TypeScript are increasingly expected; (2) a formal Bachelor's degree, which 67% of postings explicitly require or prefer. Your Diploma is strong technical credentials, but some recruiters may filter based on the degree requirement. Immediate wins: add REST API terminology to your resume, pursue AWS Cloud Practitioner cert (4–5 weeks), and learn TypeScript fundamentals (1 week). Medium-term: build Go and React projects to round out full-stack skills. Long-term: consider a part-time online Bachelor's degree to remove the credential barrier. With these additions, you'll be highly competitive for mid-level and senior IC roles within 6–12 months.
